video.title: 8 Best ChatGPT Tools to Make Money With (Ranked)

summary: Chris Koerner ranks eight ChatGPT models/products from worst to best (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Sora, GPT-4.5, Deep Research, o3/o4-mini, ChatGPT Agent, gpt-oss), explains each and suggests ways to monetise them, then adds GPT-5 as a 'number 0.5'. Cheap models suit commoditised wrapper services (bulk descriptions, captions, chatbots, cold email), while more specialised capabilities (deep research consulting, technical services, agent implementations) command higher prices. His top pick is implementing the open-weight gpt-oss privately on company servers for big setup fees plus monthly maintenance, because data privacy is what stops companies adopting AI. Key takeaway: specialised, measurable-ROI AI implementation beats low-skill wrapper services.

ideas.name: Private on-premise company GPT implementation (gpt-oss)
ideas.one_liner: Implement OpenAI's open-weight gpt-oss models on companies' own servers so their data never leaves the building; charge a big setup fee plus monthly maintenance.

ideas.customer: Companies, especially healthcare and finance, up to Fortune 500
ideas.problem: Firms want a GPT over their own data but distrust sending data to OpenAI
ideas.offer: Locally hosted company GPT trained/indexed on their data, with ongoing updates and help desk

price_points.label: hundreds or thousands for updates and help desk

pricing.notes: Could also price per gigabyte/terabyte. Custom model training reportedly costs $400k-$2M+ per project at incumbents.

acquisition_channels.details: Walk into companies (start with healthcare/finance); partner with someone with networking/hardware experience.

ideas.delivery: Operator installs gpt-oss locally, ingests data, then maintains and adds data; practise on own emails first.
unit_economics_claims: Upfront thousands to tens of thousands
Incumbents charge $400k-$2M+ per custom model project

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; strong demand from UK GDPR-sensitive sectors (NHS suppliers, FCA-regulated finance), though enterprise procurement is slow.

risks: Enterprise sales cycles and security requirements

tactics.name: Task log to find automation opportunities
steps: Keep a notepad at your computer for a day
Write down every non-complex task with a timestamp
At the end of the day photograph the list and upload it to ChatGPT
Ask it to help automate or outsource every task

quote.text: every time they perform a task that's not very complex, which are most of our tasks, they need to just write it down with a timestamp
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Cross-reference deep research across three AIs
steps: Run the identical deep research prompt in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude
Upload proprietary client data (e.g. sales data) for insight the internet lacks

quote.text: I always run the same prompt across at least three different AI companies so I can cross reference between the three
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Learn private GPT implementation on yourself first
steps: Ask ChatGPT how to run gpt-oss locally
Do it on your own data/emails as practice
Then sell to companies, starting with healthcare or finance
Partner with someone with networking/hardware experience

quote.text: Do it for your own data. Do it for your emails. Practice on yourself
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Charge premium while a capability is novel
steps: Launch services on new AI capabilities (e.g. Sora video) early
Price as high as possible before commoditisation
Expect prices to fall and plan to move on

quote.text: I highly encourage you to charge as much as you can while you can because I do think prices will continue going down in this industry
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Supervise agent automations as 'air traffic control'
steps: Connect inbound requests to an AI agent
Tweak automations after each fix so they break less over time

quote.text: you're just playing air traffic control and watching all these things happen and fixing things as they inevitably break
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Specialisation earns more: more specialised models (and services) command higher prices, like a heart surgeon vs a pediatrician.

quote.text: Who makes more money, the heart surgeon or the pediatrician? The heart surgeon, he's more specialized
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Services whose ROI is clear and measurable (coding, labour replacement) are easier to price than subjective ones like strategy.

quote.text: how do you charge someone for better big picture thinking? Results here can be subjective, which kind of makes it harder to defend your pricing
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: The 80/20 pitch: 80% cheaper and 80% as good is an easy bet for companies.

quote.text: 80% cheaper, 80% is good. What company wouldn't take a flyer on that bet
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Proprietary client data is what makes AI research uniquely valuable.

quote.text: if you really want to have it do magical things, you upload it proprietary data from you or from a business owner
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Data privacy is the blocker for enterprise AI adoption; local models remove it and create an implementation market.

quote.text: If they do know how to implement it, they're probably not implementing it because of these data privacy concerns that are now gone
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Being embedded with a client creates high switching costs and repeat AI work.

quote.text: once you're embedded with these companies, they're going to go for you for everything AI because the switching costs for them are very, very high
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use the cheapest adequate model for wrappers; extra cost of premium models is not proportional to quality.

quote.text: the additional expense is not proportional to the additional quality that you get out of it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Agents will make existing staff superhuman rather than cause mass layoffs, cutting future hiring.

quote.text: I think it's the thing that's going to turn all of their employees into superhumans
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Thinking on your feet becomes more valuable as everyone relies on AI answers.

quote.text: I think a lot of these models are going to make people that can think on their feet a lot more valuable
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner
